body: Minor issue.... Technically, calling `_encode_buffer_bins` after `_encode_buffer_glb` will cause buffers 1 and above to be written twice. But since no application currently uses more than one buffer, it probably doesn't matter, and the harm is pretty low: it just writes the same file twice. We don't need to fix this part right now.

`unlikely(p_state->buffers.size() > 1` is an incorrect check. We should allow the internal buffer to be used as long as it is less than UINT32_MAX.

The problem probably is that `_encode_buffer_glb` has an off-by-one error in the for loop:
```
for (GLTFBufferIndex i = 1; i < p_state->buffers.size() - 1; i++) {
```
should be
```
for (GLTFBufferIndex i = 1; i < p_state->buffers.size(); i++) {
```
same as `_encode_buffer_bins`, but starting at index 1.

After adding to the byteLength and uri fields to each buffer, the UTF string will grow by up to `(60 + 4 * p_path.size()) * p_state->buffers.size()` bytes - we may want to subtract this from the `UINT32_MAX` constant above.

I got this 60 number by calculating length `{"byteLength": 12345678901234567890, "uri": "1234567890"}, ` . and assuming 4 bytes per character (if my filename is all emojis or something) it's kind of overkill, but better safe than sorry.

As a user, if I want to guarantee that no .bin file is generated, I would need to first check a bunch of conditions, such as if the buffer length is less than something, otherwise if I only reference the generated .glb (for example, if I upload it somewhere that expects everything self-contained), I could end up copying a broken .glb.

A user's only choice would be to check `p_state->json).to_json_string()` and roughly approximate 2*32 less the header size to see if Godot might split it into a separate file... it is highly unlikely that the json will take 1 GB (but technically you can't know this for certain)

I do understand for usecases like exporting a scene as glb from the editor, this case makes sense to generate the extra .bin file, so this is fine for that purpose.

If it's impossible to export a single self-contained `.glb`, isn't it better to export 2 files than to fail? The user can check for the existence of a `.bin` after export.

However, if a single self-contained `.glb` or error is desired, there is another option: You can export an in-memory buffer, and save that buffer to disk. This way, runtimes that need that option do still have it.
`.glb` files will contain compact JSON, so won't have spaces in them.

Yeah I don't see a way to fix this without making the code messier, and it's mostly a theoretical issue, which isn't really even a problem, it's just a slight reduction in performance compared to the best possible.
No it is better to fail

I'm confused as to why this would be needed at all. The JSON only grows after the `if (unlikely(file_length_with_buffer > (uint64_t)UINT32_MAX)) {` check passes, after which we re-calculate the size values directly from the new JSON. If the `if (unlikely(file_length_with_buffer > (uint64_t)UINT32_MAX)) {` check fails (less than max), then we don't modify the JSON after that - it just gets stored as-is.
@fire What should we tell the user who opened issue #70973 then?
yeah you're right, I'm not sure what I was trying to figure out.

Most of this PR is good. It shouldn't segfault.

Also, I think the behavior of writing glb + bin is fine in the editor.

Personally I'm not sure it needs to fail. Perhaps we just need to document this behavior in the API docs (as well as how the behavior of .glb vs .gltf depends on file extension) and explain how to check if the buffer 0 size + length of json is 4 GB, before calling write to filesystem.
